t1.titulo: Vocabulary and steps for shopping online
t1.descripcion:
In this lesson you will learn the essential vocabulary for shopping online and the typical steps of an online purchase.

• Before buying, look for the product in the online store and add it to the cart.
• You must create an account or register with your email address.
• Choose the payment method: credit card, PayPal, bank transfer or cash on delivery.
• Check the shipping costs and the delivery time before confirming the order.
• Once the order is placed, you will receive a confirmation email with the tracking number.
• You can track the shipment from your account or with the link they send you.
• If the product does not convince you, you have the right to return it within the legal period (usually 14 days).

📌 IMPORTANT NOTE: In Spain, e-commerce law requires informing about the right of withdrawal. Always keep the order confirmation and the proof of payment.

❌ COMMON MISTAKE: Chinese speakers often say *“hacer un comprar”* instead of *“hacer una compra”*. Remember that “compra” is the noun and “comprar” the verb.
ejemplos: Añade el producto al carrito y luego ve a la caja.
Para comprar online, primero tienes que registrarte.
Prefiero pagar con tarjeta de crédito por seguridad.
El plazo de entrega es de tres a cinco días laborables.
Guarda el correo de confirmación por si acaso.

t4.descripcion:
Learn about the most common payment methods for online purchases and how to protect your data.

• The usual payment methods are: credit/debit card, PayPal, bank transfer, and cash on delivery.
• Credit card is fast, but you should check that the website is secure (https, padlock).
• PayPal offers buyer protection and does not share your bank details with the seller.
• Bank transfer is slower and does not always offer guarantees.
• Cash on delivery means paying when you receive the package; sometimes there is a surcharge.
• Never send cash or share passwords.
• Use strong passwords and enable two-step verification.
• Check your card transactions regularly.

📌 IMPORTANT NOTE: In Spain, online stores are required to inform about accepted payment methods and any additional costs before completing the purchase.

❌ COMMON MISTAKE: Chinese speakers sometimes forget the preposition “con” when saying *“pagar la tarjeta de crédito”*. The correct form is “pagar con tarjeta” or “pagar con la tarjeta”.
ejemplos: ¿Puedo pagar con PayPal?
Es más seguro pagar con tarjeta que con transferencia.
El pago contra reembolso tiene un recargo de 3 euros.
Comprueba que la página web tiene el candado de seguridad.
No compartas tu contraseña con nadie.

t2.descripcion:
Learn how to manage returns and exchanges when shopping online.

• If you don't like the product or it doesn't fit you well, you can request a return.
• You normally have 14 calendar days from receipt to return it.
• You must fill out a return form on the website or contact customer service.
• The product must be in its original packaging and unused.
• Some sellers offer free returns; others charge shipping costs.
• If the item is defective, the seller must bear the costs.
• You can ask for an exchange for another size or color if available.
• The refund is made to the same payment method used, normally within a few days.

📌 IMPORTANT NOTE: Spanish law considers a “producto defectuoso” to be one that does not match the description or does not work correctly. In that case, you have the right to repair, replacement, price reduction or termination of the contract.

❌ COMMON MISTAKE: Chinese speakers sometimes confuse “devolución” (退货) with “cambio” (换货). Remember that “devolver” implies getting your money back, while “cambiar” is replacing the product with another one.
ejemplos: Quiero devolver estos pantalones porque me quedan grandes.
El formulario de devolución está en la página web.
Si el producto está defectuoso, la devolución es gratuita.
¿Puedo cambiar este libro por otro título?
El reembolso se hará en un plazo de 5 días.

t3.descripcion:
Learn how to file a complaint when something goes wrong with an online purchase.

• If you have a problem, first contact customer service.
• You can do this by phone, email or live chat.
• Explain the problem clearly and provide evidence: order number, photos, emails.
• If you do not receive a satisfactory response, you can file a formal complaint.
• In Spain, many stores have official complaint forms.
• You can also go to a municipal consumer information office (OMIC).
• If the purchase was online, you can use the European dispute resolution platform.
• Keep all communication in writing.

📌 IMPORTANT NOTE: The phrase “poner una reclamación” is the most common in Spain. In Latin America, “hacer una reclamación” or “presentar un reclamo” are used more.

❌ COMMON ERROR: Chinese speakers often say *“hacer una queja”* when they mean “presentar una reclamación”. “Queja” is an informal protest; “reclamación” is a formal procedure.
ejemplos: Voy a poner una reclamación porque el pedido llegó roto.
Contacta con atención al cliente y explica el problema.
Adjunta una foto del producto defectuoso en el correo.
Si no contestan, puedes ir a la OMIC.
Guarda todos los correos como prueba.
